Maladaptive Strategies.value: Situations that make me feel strong emotions
I think about how life would have been different if the event had not occurred
Any situation that might involve disagreement or confrontation

Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try

Negative Appraisals.value: Somebody else would not have gotten into this situation
I have lost my connection to my community and culture
I have permanently changed for the worse

vignette: Akua had been a police officer in a busy urban precinct for nearly a decade when she was sexually assaulted by a fellow officer during a night shift three years ago. The event itself is still fragmented in her memory - there are moments of searing clarity, others that remain stubbornly hazy. What Akua recalls with visceral precision is the sound of her own voice whispering "no", and the sensation of her attacker's hands pinning her wrists to the floor. She remembers feeling a wave of shame wash over her as he leaned in close, his breath hot against her ear. The days that followed were a blur of confusion and self-blame. Akua couldn't shake the thought that she had somehow brought this on herself - that if only she'd been more vigilant, or less trusting, it wouldn't have happened. She found herself constantly replaying the events leading up to the assault in her mind, wondering what she might have done differently. These ruminations were laced with a deep-seated anger, not just towards her attacker, but also towards herself for being so foolish. As the weeks turned into months, Akua started avoiding situations that might stir up strong emotions - social gatherings, family events, even simple conversations with colleagues. She felt like she was walking on eggshells, never knowing when some innocuous comment or gesture might trigger a memory and send her tumbling back into that dark night. When memories did surface, they brought with them a wave of physical pain - a sharp ache in her wrists, a dull throb in her lower back. These somatic echoes left Akua breathless and disoriented. Her relationships began to suffer as she withdrew further and further from the world around her. Her husband, Kofi, tried to be supportive, but Akua found herself pushing him away - fearful of his touch, anxious about being alone with him. She felt like a ghost hovering at the edge of their marriage, unable to fully engage or connect. Akua's work as a police officer also started to unravel. She stopped attending community events, avoiding any situation that might involve confrontation or disagreement. Her colleagues noticed her growing isolation and began to whisper among themselves - "she's lost her edge", "she's not the same officer she used to be". Akua knew they were right - she had lost her sense of purpose, her connection to the community she was sworn to protect. Lately, Akua has been plagued by a creeping sense of permanence - that this trauma has forever altered her in some fundamental way. She sees herself as damaged goods, irreparably broken. When memories surface, they bring with them an overwhelming rage - not just towards her attacker, but also towards the world for moving on without her. It was only when Akua's captain called her into his office to discuss a performance review that she realized just how far she'd fallen. He gently pointed out her declining attendance record, her lack of engagement with colleagues and community members alike. Something about this conversation - maybe it was the quiet concern in his voice, or the genuine interest he showed in her well-being - made Akua realize that she couldn't keep running from her demons forever. As she sat across from him, feeling a mix of shame and desperation wash over her, Akua knew that she needed help. She was afraid of confronting the memories and emotions she'd been avoiding for so long, but more than that, she was terrified of losing herself completely - of disappearing into this darkness without ever finding her way back out.
